title: Book Three · Chapter 18: The Rolling Counters
story:
Another week passes. On Tuesday, the teacher brings a bag of small coloured counters.

She empties some onto the front desk. A few roll toward the edge. She catches them with her book.

“For today's maths,” she says.

Each pair needs twenty counters. Ronan and Anna get ten red ones and ten white ones. They put them between their books.

The teacher draws three bags on the board. Each has a different mix of colours.

“Which bag gives the best chance of a red counter?” she asks.

The first question is easy. The next needs three groups of counters.

Ronan moves five to the left. Anna puts five more near the ruler. One white counter rolls under her book.

“We have nineteen,” she says.

“Twenty.”

He lifts the book and finds it. She laughs and puts it back.

Behind them, something drops. A boy bends down to find a red counter. Across the room, another counter rolls off a desk.

Ronan looks at the smooth little shapes. Then he looks at a sheet of spare paper in his book.

He folds one edge up. He folds the other edges too. At each corner, he pinches the paper flat.

Soon he has a shallow paper tray. It is not very neat, but its sides stay up.

He puts two counters inside and pushes them. They reach the paper edge and stop.

Anna moves the others into the tray.

“A house for twenty,” she says.

“No stairs. They can't fall down.”

They finish the question. Anna checks the numbers. Ronan moves each group back into the tray.

Kai turns round from the next desk. He looks at the folded paper.

“Can I have one?”

“Have you got spare paper?”

Kai takes out a sheet. Ronan shows him the first fold. Kai folds the next side himself.

His first corner opens. He presses it flat again.

The teacher walks past and stops. She looks at the counters inside Ronan's tray.

“That keeps them together.”

“They roll,” Ronan says.

“I noticed.”

She smiles and goes to the next desk.

At the end of the lesson, everyone counts their twenty counters back into the bag. Ronan lifts the tray with both hands.

“Hold the bag open,” he tells Anna.

She does. He tips one corner down, and the counters slide into the opening.

No one has to look under their desk.

Kai brings his tray over. One corner is bent, but all his counters are inside.

“Mine has a small door,” he says.

Ronan presses the corner shut.

“Not now.”

At lunch, Kai puts his empty tray beside his food. He drops a piece of carrot into it.

“Twenty carrots?” Ronan asks.

“One is enough.”

Ronan puts his own tray inside his book. The folds stay in the paper after he closes it.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

counter＝计算用的小筹码；chance＝机会、可能性；shallow＝浅的；tray＝浅盘、托盘。

## 理解问题

1. 大家使用小筹码时遇到什么实际问题？
2. Ronan怎样解决这个问题？Kai是否完全由Ronan代做了自己的纸盘？

## 读句子

**He folds one edge up.**

拆开看：He / folds / one edge up.

他／折起／纸的一条边。
